title: Confirm a veto before it voids
statement: Before one judge sample's critical failure voids a whole lesson, draw more samples and let the veto stand only when most of them fail.
example: A single sample hard-vetoed about 2 of 126 otherwise fine lessons to 0.0 in each run.
detail: In an AP evaluator's lesson check, one lesson-level sample occasionally failed every critical score on an otherwise fine lesson, and because those scores are critical it hard-vetoed the lesson to 0.0, on about 2 of 126 lessons per run. The fix draws up to 3 samples only when the first reports a critical failure and trusts the veto only if a strict majority of the available samples fail; when samples disagree, the result carries a low-confidence flag and is treated as needing review. When confirmation samples errored the rule fell back to a single-sample veto, until a guard for fewer than 2 usable samples returned the failure as low-confidence instead. A flagged verdict is treated as needing review, not as a precise score.
against: It was validated on a 14-item sample run 3 times during a provider outage, and a majority of samples shows consistency, not correctness. A confirmed failure keeps one whole sample rather than voting score by score, so its other scores rest on that one sample.

evidence.quote: A single Phase-2 lesson-level sample occasionally tanks ALL critical metrics (factual/educational/stimulus) on an otherwise-fine lesson; because they're critical that hard-vetoes the bundle to overall 0.0 (~2/126 lessons per run,
only if it reports a critical failure do we draw up to 3 samples and require a strict majority of AVAILABLE samples to fail before trusting the veto.

+ low_confidence flag on the result when confirmation samples disagree (some pass, some fail) — a genuinely borderline lesson whose overall score is not reliable; treat as needs-review instead of forcing a precise number.
- Consensus degenerated to a single-sample veto when all confirmation samples errored
Added a <2-sample guard that returns the failure as low_confidence instead of a confirmed hard-veto.
Validated on a 14-item sample x3 (during a live Gemini 503 storm)

Documented that the confirmed-fail path intentionally returns ONE coherent sample rather than reconciling non-critical metrics across samples (per-metric voting would decouple each score from its own reasoning text).
